provenance.notes: Ext family batch. One-crew painters with a truck magnet; prep, colour and winter cabinet work carry the kit. No paint brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: House painting prep, step by step
pageStructurePlus.contains: Washing, scraping, sanding, caulking gaps, priming bare wood, masking windows and plants, and the prep a cheap painting bid skips
pageStructurePlus.why: Two painting quotes for the same house differ mostly in prep. Showing the steps is how a painter explains the higher number.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Sample boards on the wall, body-trim-door combinations, sheen choices, historic palettes, HOA approval, and how a colour visit is booked
pageStructurePlus.why: Colour is the decision that stalls a painting job for weeks. Offering help with it moves the start date forward.

pageStructurePlus.section: Coatings and sheen in plain words
pageStructurePlus.contains: Acrylic versus oil, flat, satin and gloss, primer types, number of coats, and how long a repaint lasts on wood, stucco, brick and fiber cement
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners can't compare bids that list different products. A plain explainer makes the painter's spec the standard.

pageStructurePlus.section: Rotten trim and carpentry before painting
pageStructurePlus.contains: Rotted fascia, sills, corner boards and siding boards, how carpentry is priced per piece, and why painting over rot fails
pageStructurePlus.why: Rot found on ladder day becomes an argument unless it was explained first. Priced carpentry also lifts the job total.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Kitchen cabinet painting with doors sprayed off-site, interior rooms, trim and stair rails, booked for the cold months
pageStructurePlus.why: Exterior painters go quiet in winter. Cabinet and interior work keeps the crew paid and sells to the same happy customers.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Temperature and dew limits, rain days, which side gets painted first, how long a house takes, and how rain delays are communicated
pageStructurePlus.why: The question every customer asks after signing is 'when'. A clear weather policy saves calls on every job.

designDirections.name: Fresh Coat
designDirections.bestFor: One-crew house painters who win on a quick estimate and a friendly owner
designDirections.whyItFits: Teal and tangerine feel like fresh paint chips, and the humanist type reads like a person, not a franchise. The estimate button stays loud.

designDirections.name: Same House, New Colour
designDirections.bestFor: Painting companies with a library of peeling-to-finished houses sorted by colour and siding type
designDirections.headlineSample: Exterior painting that holds up on {City} houses
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. A calm evergreen frame doesn't fight the house colours in the gallery, and the before-after hero shows the peeling trim beside the new coat.

designDirections.name: Period Colours
designDirections.bestFor: Painters restoring Victorians, craftsman bungalows and historic district homes with multi-colour schemes
designDirections.headlineSample: Painting {City}'s historic homes, one careful coat at a time
designDirections.whyItFits: Brick, linen and a typewriter slab feel like a restoration journal, which suits long write-ups of one old house and its colour scheme.

openers.line: Your truck magnet has a number but your Google listing has no website. A neighbour who saw the house you painted wants to look you up before calling, and there's nowhere to land.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Note if the truck appears in any job post. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where that truck magnet could point: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your profile is a Facebook page. Someone deciding between three house painters wants your prep steps and a colour help page, and a feed scatters both.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest house they posted.
openers.linkLine: A house painting page built for that decision: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your painting site still shows a builder banner and last year's spring special. People hiring a painter for a whole house want to know the business is active this season.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a free-host banner, an expired offer or a stale copyright year. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same painting company, current and fast: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your house painting gallery loads as a long column of tiny thumbnails on my phone. Colour is the whole sale, and people judge it on a phone screen.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your painting gallery, rebuilt to show colour on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Booking a painting estimate with you means a phone call during work hours. People walk around the house on Sunday deciding to repaint and would rather send the address and a few notes then.
openers.hook: Check the profile, listing and any site for an estimate form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A painting estimate request that asks storeys, siding and colour: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your before-and-after house colour changes sell painting better than any advert could. Right now they scroll past between job-site selfies.
openers.hook: Pick two colour transformations on their grid you can describe by colour. Use one in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Your house colour changes, side by side: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews keep praising how carefully your crew masked windows and covered plants. That's exactly what scares people about hiring painters, and it isn't on any page.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about prep, cleanup or care. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those painting reviews next to the prep they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Exterior painting calendars fill in late winter for spring and summer. The painters who are easy to find in February start the season booked.
openers.hook: Use from January to March. Name the month in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the painting season fills: {demo-link}

openers.line: When it's too cold to paint outside, kitchen cabinet painting keeps crews busy. If you do it, nobody searching for cabinet painters in {City} can tell.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted cabinets or interiors. Note the post date and the cabinet colour.
openers.linkLine: A cabinet painting page for your slow months: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the help-wanted post for painters. Experienced brush hands look at a painting company's finished houses before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or story. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A painting company page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: You paint houses all over {City} and nearby, but there's no page that tells someone in {Neighborhood} you work there. 'House painters' plus the town is what gets typed.
openers.hook: Find towns in their posts or reviews. Use the one furthest from their base.
openers.linkLine: A house painting page for each town: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you split a house painting job into a deposit and a final payment, or offer a plan, say it on a page. People want to know how paying a painter works before they ask for a number.
openers.hook: Only if they mention payment terms or financing anywhere. Otherwise skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: How paying for a painting job works, explained up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: Scraping paint on older houses means lead dust, and careful buyers ask about it. Your painting licence and lead-safe certification belong on a page they can check.
openers.hook: Check the state registry and any lead-safe certification they mention. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence and lead-safe painting on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your painting work spreads street to street once a house looks good. Even a neighbour's recommendation gets searched before the call, and right now there's nothing to find.
openers.hook: Look for reviews like 'saw the house down the road' or 'neighbour recommended'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a painting referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted has crisp trim lines and a colour that suits the house. A job like that should greet visitors, not sit three weeks down the feed.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished house on their grid and name it: body colour, trim colour, and the street if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That painting job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted has clean trim lines, nice work.

I was looking for house painters in {City} and found {Business Name} on social, but no site where someone can see your prep or ask for an estimate. I sketched out a sample painting site to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like to see it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, circling back in case my message got lost under estimates. Here's the sample house painting site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It walks through your prep step by step, has a colour help page, a winter cabinet painting page and an estimate request that asks storeys and siding type. If it's not for you, just say and I'll drop it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for painting contractors in {City}. I sent you a note a couple of days ago, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} that shows your painting prep, colour help and a cabinet page for winter, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you make of it?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many town and service pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and edits. For a painter your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, roughly what one small exterior repaint brings in."
"Could I show you around it for ten minutes, maybe one evening this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. We start when it clears, and it'll be live before the spring painting rush."

objections.objection: My truck and yard signs bring in enough work.
objections.handler: "They clearly work. The people who see the truck still search your name before calling. Right now they find a Facebook page; the site is where that sign pays off."

objections.objection: Everyone just wants the lowest painting bid.
objections.handler: "Some do. The prep page is for the ones comparing what's in the bid: scraping, priming, caulk, coats. That's what makes your number look fair."
"That's the month to build it. The cabinet page brings in winter work now, and the exterior pages are ready when people plan spring painting."

objections.objection: I'm on a lead app already.
objections.handler: "Those leads go to several painters at once. Your own site sends that homeowner straight to you, and you don't pay per lead."

objections.objection: My nephew is doing my website.
objections.handler: "Great, that's cheaper. Happy to pass along the prep page and the estimate form. If it stalls before spring, my offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a gallery, a prep page, colour help and an estimate form. Less than one small house."

email.subject: Painting site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, {Your Name} here. I build websites for house painters in {City} and put together a sample for {Business Name}, prep page, colour help and all. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm clearing out old demos on Friday, including the {Business Name} painting one.

Should I keep it up for you? A yes or no is plenty.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, painting season is coming up and calendars around {City} are starting to fill. You came to mind.

The painting site is still here and the price hasn't moved. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one small exterior repaint, not an hourly rate.
Price the gallery by number of houses, sorted by colour and siding type, not by page count.
The prep and coatings pages are what justify their price; quote them as one line and never skip them.
Add the cabinet painting page only for painters who actually spray cabinets; it's a winter revenue line for them.
Colour consultation booking is its own line when they charge for colour visits.
Keep the care plan small; painters change offers seasonally and need edits more than features.

lineItems.description: Max with a step-by-step prep sequence for each siding type and a plain sheen chart.

lineItems.item: Estimate request with storeys and siding fields
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload of problem areas, colour-help checkbox and a preferred start month.
Max when it takes a paid colour visit booking with deposit and shows past colour schemes by house style.
Max with its own gallery, a cabinet door count form and a winter booking offer.
Max with lead-safe process details, multi-colour scheme examples and district approval notes.
Max when each town page shows houses painted there and common siding types on its streets.
Max when the prep page, estimate form and colour page are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Colour transformation shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Before you start the next big colour change, I shoot the house as it is, then again after the last trim coat, same angles. That pair sells your next painting job."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, booked around their next colour-change house.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts of painted houses
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every finished house goes on your Google profile with the colours and the town, so the map shows a busy painter instead of last spring's post."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after the final painting walk
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After the final walk-around and touch-ups, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review while they're standing in the yard admiring the house."

whatElseYouSell.name: Yard signs and truck graphics for painters
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A 'freshly painted by' yard sign stays up a week after the crew leaves. With the site on it, the fresh paint keeps selling."

whatElseYouSell.name: Street postcards after each painted house
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Houses on a street often need painting at the same time. A postcard of the neighbour's new colours reaches people already eyeing their own peeling trim."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once there are houses on the site.

whatElseYouSell.name: Winter cabinet painting campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A November push to past exterior customers offering cabinet painting fills the cold months with indoor work from people who already trust the crew."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, run in November.

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring booking push for exterior repaints
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A late-winter offer for early spring start dates fills the first weeks of exterior painting season before every crew in town is booked."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in January, run in February.

whatElseYouSell.name: Colour lookbook for realtors and stagers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short lookbook of houses you've repainted, with the colour schemes, puts your painting company in front of agents prepping listings."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the gallery has several houses.

withoutAI.route: Carpenters who fix rot before you paint
withoutAI.whoPays: The carpenter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every painting job turns up rotten trim. The carpenter you call for it needs a site, and they meet homeowners who need a painter next."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Carpentry and painting run in sequence; referrals flow both ways.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The pressure washer who cleans the house before you paint needs a booking site. You already send them work."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: House washing is a natural pre-painting step; the painter's referral is a warm door.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The independent paint store where you buy sees every painter and DIYer in town. Introduce me and I'll build their colour and contractor-finder pages."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Independent paint stores have budgets and want contractors to stay loyal.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The colour consultant who picks your customers' house colours needs a portfolio site, and your painting jobs are their best examples."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers and painters share clients; a painter's referral carries weight.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Stagers tell sellers to repaint the front door and trim before listing. They need a site, and they need a painter they trust."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Stagers buy credibility and send steady pre-listing painting jobs.

withoutAI.whoPays: The kitchen shop, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Kitchen shops send customers who want painted cabinets rather than new ones. They need a better site, and your cabinet painting page links to them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Overlapping kitchen customers without competing products.

withAI.route: Colour match assistant for the paint store
withAI.pitchLine: "Customers upload a shot of their house and the store's assistant suggests body and trim colours from its own fan deck, then lists local painters."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells more paint and sends exterior painting work to the client.

withAI.route: Listing photo exterior refresh preview for agents
withAI.pitchLine: "Agents upload the front of a listing and see it repainted in a couple of colour schemes, labelled as a preview, with the painter's number beside it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents use it to talk sellers into a repaint; the painter gets the job.

withAI.route: House wash booking bot for the pressure washer
withAI.pitchLine: "The pressure washer who preps your painting jobs misses bookings at night. An assistant quotes house washes by size and books them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Configuration of a booking flow you know, through a warm referral.

withAI.pitchLine: "Consultants get a tool that drafts exterior colour moodboards from a house photo and the client's likes, ready for them to refine."
withAI.whyItWorks: Consultants save hours per client; the painting client gets the jobs.

withAI.pitchLine: "The carpenter you call for rotted sills gets a tool that drafts a repair quote from a few shots, so your painting jobs don't wait on their paperwork."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster carpentry quotes mean faster painting starts.

withAI.pitchLine: "Townhome HOAs repaint buildings in cycles. An assistant tracks which buildings are due, drafts the notices and routes the bids to one painting contractor."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers juggle repaint schedules by spreadsheet; the painter gets planned work.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for painting estimates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Up a ladder with a brush in hand? The caller gets a text asking for the address and whether it's exterior, interior or cabinets, and you ring back between coats."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: House painting price range by size and storeys
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner picks square footage, storeys and siding type and sees a painting range, so the estimate visit starts with realistic expectations."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their pricing by size and siding, trim adders and the smallest job they take.

softwareAI.name: Rain-delay texts to booked customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When rain pushes a house painting day, every affected customer gets a text with the new date in one tap, instead of ten phone calls at dawn."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their schedule and the customer list for the week.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and completion invoicing for painting jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit to hold the start date, balance after the touch-up walk, both sent automatically so the painter isn't chasing cheques."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Paint colour preview on the customer's house
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners upload a shot of their house and try body, trim and door colours on it, so the painting decision stops stalling on colour."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the colour lines they use. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; previews are labelled as previews.

softwareAI.name: Painted-house review responses
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every new review about a painted house gets a reply drafted that mentions the colours and the crew by name, ready to approve between coats."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review asks. Needs a dozen past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Painting estimate builder with prep line items
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick the sides, the prep level and the coats, and a clean painting estimate prints with each prep step listed, so it beats the one-line bid next door."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their estimate template and production rates.

softwareAI.name: Painting job calendar with weather view
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every booked house painting job on one calendar next to the forecast, so you see which starts are at risk before the crew loads the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job list and crew count.

softwareAI.name: Square footage draft from house photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From street shots and an aerial view it drafts paintable wall area, trim length and window count for the painter to check before quoting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past jobs with measured areas. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Colour record by address
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every house you paint is saved with the exact colours and sheens, so a touch-up years later, or the neighbour who wants 'the same blue', is instant."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs past job colour notes.

softwareAI.name: Painter chatbot for prep, sheen and timing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'satin or flat for my siding' and 'how long will you be at my house' at night, from your painting notes, and books the estimate."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their coatings notes and current lead time. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Repaint reminder for older paint jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers whose house you painted years ago get a note in late winter to check the south side and the trim, with a touch-up or repaint offer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a customer list with paint dates.

softwareAI.name: Cabinet painting quote from kitchen photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner uploads kitchen shots and it counts doors and drawers and drafts a cabinet painting range for you to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, before winter. Needs their price per door and drawer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew daily log with prep checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The lead painter ticks off washing, scraping, priming and caulking per side with a shot each, so you see every house without driving there."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they run two crews. Needs their prep checklist.

softwareAI.name: Spoken walk-around to painting notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the house saying which sides peel and where the rot is, and the painting estimate builder fills in from what you said."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the estimate builder. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Paint and materials cost tracker per house
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Log gallons, caulk and crew hours per painting job and see which house types actually pay, and which you underbid."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of receipts and crew hours.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with colour sign-off
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners sign off on body and trim colours, see their painting start date and rain delays, and pay the deposit in one place."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the job calendar running first.

softwareAI.name: Painting blog and town page writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A monthly house painting page, like the best colours for brick ranches in {Neighborhood}, drafted from your jobs and approved by you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Subcontract painter onboarding pack
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New painters and subs get your prep standards, safety rules and insurance paperwork on their phone before day one."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they add subs. Needs their standards written down once.

softwareAI.name: Painter applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Painter applicants say whether they can cut a clean line, run a sprayer and climb a forty-foot ladder, before you spend a call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: When they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a painting estimate builder that itemises prep for one painter. Most painters still write a one-line bid by hand."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first painter taught you the production rates and paid for it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Contractor finder for an independent paint store group
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A find-a-painter page across your stores sends homeowners to the painting contractors with house accounts, and keeps them buying from you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Paint stores live on contractor accounts and spend on loyalty.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give member painters a template with a prep page, colour help and an estimate form as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One deal reaches many painting owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with house painter clients rebuild the same pages. License my painting template with prep and colour pages done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell; you supply the finished trade part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "House painting franchises need territory pages with local jobs and estimate routing. One build, many owners."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Colour preview tool licensed to paint retailers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The house colour preview built for one painter works for any paint counter: customers try colours on their own house and leave with a painter's name."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Retailers want tools that move paint; you've already built it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: HOA repaint program portal for management firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community the firm manages gets an approved colour palette page, repaint schedule and painter request form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Firms managing many HOAs buy once and roll out everywhere.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Trade school painting program career pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Painting apprenticeship programs need pages that show students real house painting careers and local employers. Your client can be the first."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools fund recruitment pages; painters need hires.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly note on paint, caulk and labour cost trends that painting contractors report, so their bids keep up."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built only from shared data; it never claims more than painters report.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Cabinet painting add-on kit for painters elsewhere
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The winter cabinet painting page, quote tool and campaign, packaged for exterior painters in any cold-weather city."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every northern painter has the same slow winter.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Exclusive painter in the next town
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A house painter in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Promise one painting company per town. When {City} is done, the best one-crew painter in the next town gets the same demo."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusivity sells; the template carries over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Lots of painters have a half-finished site someone else started. I can finish it on a painting template that's already live."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already decided to buy.

upsellLadder.offer: Painting site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The painting site and care plan sit on one contract, so swapping the spring offer for the cabinet offer is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks after the final painting walk
upsellLadder.trigger: The first house painted since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "That house you just finished is a glowing review waiting. Let's ask every customer at the final walk."

upsellLadder.trigger: They book a house with a big colour change.
upsellLadder.line: "That colour change you're starting next week is your best before-and-after. Let's shoot both ends of the painting job."

upsellLadder.trigger: A rainy week forces them to call every booked painting customer.
upsellLadder.line: "Last week's rain cost you a morning of calls. Next time it's one tap."

upsellLadder.offer: Paint colour preview on the customer's house
upsellLadder.trigger: A signed painting job stalls on colour choice.
upsellLadder.line: "That job waiting on a colour decision starts sooner if they see their own house in each colour."

upsellLadder.trigger: The exterior calendar thins out as the weather turns cold.
upsellLadder.line: "Your exterior painting season is ending. Let's fill winter with cabinets for customers who already love your work."

upsellLadder.offer: Painting job calendar with weather view
upsellLadder.trigger: They add a second painting crew.
upsellLadder.line: "Two painting crews and the weather need one calendar. Let's stop guessing which starts will slip."
